newsitem.title: GERMANY: 50,000 flock to fair on Hamburg's frozen lake.
newsitem.headline: 50,000 flock to fair on Hamburg's frozen lake.

text.p: Tens of thousands of people flocked to Hamburg's frozen-over Alster lake on Saturday to go strolling, skating and skiing on the thick ice surface in sub-zero temperatures.

Police said about 50,000 people turned up on the lake, one of Hamburg city-centre's most famous landmarks, where authorities gave the go-ahead for 150 food and drink stands to be set up for the second year running.

People from Hamburg and day-trippers from the surrounding area thronged the stalls, drinking mulled wine and munching bratwurst while catching a rare view of the snow-covered city from the middle of the lake.

Others walked dogs, cycled, pulled children along on sledges and played ice hockey -- wrapped up warmly with the daytime temperature at about minus two Celsius (28F) -- on the 15-cm (six inch) thick frozen surface of lake in the northern port city.
Temperatures have remained below zero for the last two weeks across northern Germany, and at night have dipped as low as minus 24 C degrees Celsius (-11F) in parts of eastern Germany.

Before last winter, when the city-centre Alster basin froze over for several weeks, the ice had been too thin to walk on since 1991. Before that, there had not been ice thick enough to tread on for more than ten years.
